unite_adi: REGULAR UPPER SECONDARY-YEAR 11-LEVEL: B1.3 THEME 1: SCHOOL LIFE & EDUCATION

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students will create a project titled "School Life and Education Around the World, focusing on the sub-themes of comparing different types of schools, education systems, and national days or celebrations related to education. Students will begin by researching and comparing different types of schools, such as public, private, and vocational institutions, highlighting their unique features and approaches to education. They will explore and compare education systems in various countries, discussing similarities and differences in teaching methods, curriculum structures, and student outcomes. Additionally, students will examine how national days and celebrations, such as Republic Day, Teacher’s Day or Education Week, are observed in different cultures, reflecting on their importance in promoting education and school pride. The project will include written content, visuals, and personal reflections, and students will present their findings in class. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''school life and education with its components such as comparing different types of schools; comparing different education systems; national days and celebrations'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student of an upper secondary school in year 11 may know what school life and education, different types of schools; comparing different education systems; national days and celebrations mean in their own language as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in another language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students of an upper secondary school in year 11, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''school life and education'' in English from previous themes and/or years such as ''a teacher, a student, a headmaster, a class, a classroom, a state school, to study, to go to school and so on'' and also some structures such as ''What’s/is it/this? It’s/is a classroom. What do students do at school? They study and they learn. What are they learning now?'' in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in an upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''school life and education with its components such as comparing different types of schools; comparing different education systems; national days and celebrations'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, a contextual poster or a large picture could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss the poster and/or the picture in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (At the beginning of the academic term, there is a month-long programme revision programme of intensive revision of the themes, vocabulary, and language chunks from previous years but, before starting each new theme, such as a short revision is also carried out to support their learning process) (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective : To talk about different types of schools and different education systems in English through a discussion activity by using target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 1: Exploring School Systems through Group Discussions The teacher informs students that they work in small groups to discuss different types of schools and different education systems topics. The teacher prepares discussion topics, such as ''What makes a school modern and well-equipped?'' and ''How can schools provide equal opportunities for all students?'' writes them on small cards, and places them in a box. Each group sends one student to draw a card from the box. The group discusses the chosen question, making sure that each member contributes by using target vocabulary (e.g., diverse, challenging, collaborative) and target grammar structures such as modal verbs of deduction (e.g., The library must be an important facility for modern schools) and passive voice (e.g., Opportunities are provided to students in student-centred schools). After the discussion, the group writes their key points and conclusions, then reads them aloud to the class. The teacher listens carefully and provides constructive feedback on target vocabulary usage, grammar accuracy, and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To learn about different types of schools and education systems in English through matching words with visuals by using target vocabulary. Activity 1: Explore School Vocabulary The teacher prepares a worksheet or uses a digital platform featuring pictures of different types of schools (e.g., a traditional school, a modern school, an interactive classroom, a student-centred school). Each picture represents a specific school type or education system, with blank spaces below the pictures where students write suitable words from a provided word bank. The word bank includes target vocabulary such as diverse, traditional, challenging, flexible, collaborative, interactive, modern, student-centred, etc. with small clues next to each word to help understanding (e.g., ''Traditional'' – formal uniforms, orderly rows). For instance, a picture showing students in uniforms sitting in rows with a teacher at the blackboard matches the word ''Traditional''. After completing the activity, students take turns reading the words they wrote aloud to practice pronunciation. The teacher provides constructive and supportive feedback on pronunciation and accuracy. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
